passage: SOURCES_D row SIM03 (abstract): class-prediction performance assessed on the data used to build the rule; independent validation is required.
faulty: L2-penalised logistic regression (penalty fixed, all 2000 standardised genes, no selection) is fitted on all 120 patients; the AUC of its fitted scores for relapse_5y on those same 120 patients is the statistic. Claim holds when AUC >= 0.70.
fixed: 10-fold cross-validation (patients in the held-out fold not used in fitting or standardising); AUC of the pooled held-out scores.
estimand: Faulty: ranking quality of the model on the patients that built it. Fixed: AUC on new patients.
model_family: L2-penalised logistic regression with a fixed penalty. Chosen by me: the source names no model; fixed penalty and no selection keep the case L1.1.
sizes_note: Source sizes: not stated in what I read. 120 x 2000 = 240k values, a larger-n prognostic array study; cheap. Dependence of the error on n or p: not stated.
exploited_structure: Many more genes than patients, so training scores can separate relapse from non-relapse by chance.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: SIM03 sizes were not available to me; 16.67 = 2000 genes / 120 patients, this brief's own ratio

notes: Reserve for SIM03 L1.1. Statistic family classification (AUC): this is the source's own two-class setting (relapse as a binary prognostic class); the earlier evaluation used (L1.1, classification) too, so it is a reserve. Differs from B2B-01/02 in statistic, outcome type and sizes.
